title: docs(spec): `manifest.integrity` TSDoc stops asserting an unpack verification nobody performs
body:
**Landing path: ORDINARY `packages/spec` PR — this diff touches NO governed surface, so it is armable in the usual way and does not need a human merge.**

`docs/adr/0025-plugin-package-distribution.md` is deliberately **not** edited; the reasoning is in "Why the ADR needed no edit" below. Checked mechanically against the register rather than recalled: today's `GOVERNED_SURFACES` is `docs/adr/**` · `.claude/**` · `skills/**` · `AGENTS.md` · `CLAUDE.md`, and the four changed paths hit none of them.

Fixes #16333

`Clause-②: no` — prose only. No export added, removed or narrowed; no authorable key moved; no accept-set movement. Proven with a two-direction ablation below rather than read off a bare green.

## What was wrong

The `integrity` TSDoc said per-file re-verification at unpack is the **cloud control plane's** obligation. The cloud repo's documentary half says it is the **runtime's**. Neither side unpacks anything, so two published texts each pointed at the other and a reader of either learned that a verification exists when none does. Because this text ships inside `@objectstack/spec`'s `.d.ts`, the wrong claim reached every consumer that hovered the field.

Measured in this checkout at `3335bd35eaf47a5b2aed9120e217dafd242ff7e1`:

- `computeIntegrity` is defined at `packages/cli/src/utils/osplugin.ts` and has exactly one production caller, `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/build.ts`.
- `verifyIntegrity` has exactly one production caller, the `os plugin publish` preflight (`packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/publish.ts`).
- There is **no `os plugin install`** — `packages/cli/src/commands/plugin/` holds `build.ts`, `publish.ts`, `sign.ts` and nothing else.
- The archive reader `readTarGz`'s only production caller is that same publish path, reading back its own output. Nothing in this repo unpacks an installed artifact.

Cloud's half is **not** re-measured here; this session has no access to that repo. The cloud-side reading is inherited from #13563 and labelled as inherited, and cloud's documentary half stays with #13563 by the same ruling.

## The line anchor had drifted

The card cites `manifest.zod.ts:129-131`. At the anchor sha that range is `PluginRuntimeSchema`'s describe and `PluginPackagingSchema`. Re-located by symbol, the docblock is at **`:139-145`**, and there is a **second** one the card's line cite does not reach: the `integrity` field's own TSDoc inside `ManifestSchema`, at **`:748-753`**, carrying the same false attribution. Both are rewritten — acceptance asks that `manifest.zod.ts` no longer assert a cloud-side unpack verification, and one of the two would have left the claim shipping.

## What the TSDoc says now

- **Computed and self-checked by the publisher.** `os plugin build` computes the map; the `os plugin publish` preflight re-hashes the artifact bytes against it and refuses on digest mismatch, a declared entry with no file, or a packaged file the map does not declare (#13464). An absent map is a permissive pass — the field is `.optional()`.
- **Not re-verified at unpack.** That leg is not implemented. It is owned by the **future runtime loader** (ADR-0025 §3.5 steps 4-7), **not** by the control plane, which stores the artifact blob opaquely.
- A one-line pointer to #11331 so the enforce leg is findable when the loader is built.

## Why the ADR needed no edit

The card makes ADR correction conditional on its prose stating step 5 as **done**. It does not — it states it as **designed**:

- The ADR's own Status line already reads: *"the install flow (§3.5) ... remain unimplemented"*. That is the only implementation-status assertion in the file, and it is correct.
- The four unpack mentions are all design mood: `:118` is the §2 Decision statement, `:171` describes the bundled packaging strategy, `:236` is step 5 of the §3.5 numbered design list, and `:448` is a §5 projected consequence. None claims the step is built.
- §3.5 also **corroborates** the correction: its steps 4-7 assign download-and-verify, materialize, register and load to the installing host, never to the control plane. The old TSDoc contradicted the ADR; the new one agrees with it.

So the ADR is left alone rather than touched for thoroughness, and this PR stays off the governed path.

## Liveness ledger

The card names the ledger alongside the ADR. No row states step 5 as **done** — but two carried the same wrong owner, which acceptance ("ADR / ledger text agrees with the TSDoc") does not allow to stand:

- `packages/spec/liveness/manifest.json` — the `integrity` row's note said the leg *"remains the cloud control plane's obligation"*. Corrected to the future runtime loader.
- `packages/spec/liveness/README.md` — its note said *"nothing computes or checks them"*, stale since #13464 and contradicting the corrected TSDoc. Corrected. This cell is hand-written by design: `readme-table.mts` generates the row set and the counts, and states that the Notes content is deliberately never generated.

The row's `status` (`dead`) and `verifiedAt` (2026-08-30) are **deliberately unchanged**. This is a prose correction, not a re-measurement, and moving `verifiedAt` would falsely claim a fresh liveness reading.

## Verification

Base `3335bd35eaf47a5b2aed9120e217dafd242ff7e1`; all readings below taken at head `9fd63b161d`.

**Generated artifacts — zero movement.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` (after a real build) reports **"All 15 generated artifacts are up to date"**. `git diff --name-only BASE..HEAD` lists exactly the four changed files, none of them generated. Nothing was hand-edited and nothing needed regenerating: TSDoc feeds no artifact, only `.describe()` does, and no `.describe()` was touched.

Measured generated-artifact footprint, since the card asks for it tracked vs gitignored:

| tree | files | |
|---|---|---|
| `api-surface/` | 17 | tracked |
| `export-origins/` | 17 | tracked |
| `authorable-surface/` | 14 | tracked |
| `declaration-map/` | 14 | tracked |
| `authorable-defaults/` | 13 | tracked |
| 4 singletons + `authorable-surface.base.json` + `docs/protocol-upgrade-guide.md` | 6 | tracked |
| `content/docs/references/` | 228 | tracked |
| **`packages/spec/json-schema/`** | **1576** | **gitignored** (`.gitignore:63`) |

Tracked total is **309**, not "~14" — that figure is exactly the `authorable-surface/` shard count, which misses the other four sharded directories, the singletons, the 228-file references tree, and the whole 1576-file gitignored `json-schema/` tree.

**Clause ② — two-direction ablation, no rebuild between mutation and check.** The confound is real: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build` regenerates the gates' own baselines, so a mutate-build-check leg comes back falsely green. Avoided by mutating the **checked-in baseline** instead of the source, which needs no rebuild at all. Each leg proved its mutation reached disk by `git hash-object` differing from the HEAD blob, restored with `git checkout HEAD -- PATH`, and proved restoration by the hash returning to the HEAD blob.

| gate | leg | verdict | exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `check:api-surface` | drop a real export from the baseline | `0 breaking (removed/narrowed), 1 added` | 1 |
| `check:api-surface` | add a phantom export to the baseline | `1 breaking (removed/narrowed), 0 added` | 1 |
| `check:authorable-surface` | drop `kernel/ValidationWarning:message` | `authorable-surface/ is out of date (1 key(s) not recorded)` | 1 |
| `check:authorable-surface` | add `kernel/OsAblationPhantomDef:phantomProp` | `1 authorable key(s) disappeared from the contract` | 1 |

The two legs of each gate produce **opposite** diagnostics, so this is a real two-direction proof and not merely two reds.

One leg was **discarded as vacuous rather than banked**: a first attempt at the authorable-surface add-direction used the key `OsAblationPhantom.key`, which the gate rejected as malformed (*"cannot shard ... has no category segment"*). That red graded my fixture's shape, not the ratchet, so the leg was re-run with a well-formed key and only the re-run is reported above.

Clean verdicts on the unmutated tree, exit codes captured before any pipe:

- `check:api-surface` — exit **0**, *"public API surface + factory signatures unchanged"*
- `check:authorable-surface` — exit **0**, *"authorable-defaults/ verified against upstream 3335bd35eaf4 — 1211 default(s) unchanged"*

**Tests, typecheck, gates.**

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` — **483 files / 13136 tests passed**, lock verdict `command-exit 0`
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` — exit 0
- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --ran` — **69 derived families, 69 run, 0 UNRUN**
- `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`) — exit **0**, so the whole-repo scan is a real reading here, not a narrowing
- `pnpm check:nul-bytes` green, plus a direct control-character scan over the three edited files: no matches

**One family is NOT MEASURED, not passed.** `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits **3** — `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, because it reads built output for ~87 packages and only the `@objectstack/spec` closure was built here. Its own text says *"This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured."* CI builds everything and will measure it. (`check:doc-formula-expressions` also exited 3 at first; that one was cheap to satisfy, so `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/lint` were built and it was re-run to a real **exit 0**.)

## Out of scope, filed separately

The same false attribution lives at **five more sites** outside this card's scope, in `packages/cli` and `packages/core`. They are deliberately not touched here: editing them would pull two more packages into the verification surface for a prose card. Filed for triage rather than ridden along.
